rationale: Both independently corroborate the same critical double-seeded num_stale_output_tokens bug and the dead async_tokens_to_discard writes with matching line citations, giving strong grounding for those. Neither hits the ground truth's actual (mostly stylistic, already-resolved) inline comments, so recall is low and roughly tied for both. Y edges out on precision via explicit validate/sweep passes that rule out several borderline concerns as non-issues, plus a well-evidenced novel finding (NPU _dummy_run missing randomize_inputs) and a thorough 10-file arg_utils.py regression sweep, whereas X asserts a VLLM_CACHE_ROOT race condition that Y directly refutes with specific lock-ordering evidence, a likely false positive. X is marginally more actionable with inline code-diff fix suggestions.
